editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the terms are correct and used the same way each time (expectation value→valeur d'espérance, error mitigation→atténuation des erreurs, PEC→annulation probabiliste des erreurs, "more tightly bound"→"mieux borner"), and the text uses "tu" consistently (Découvre, Consulte).

The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The pre-flight checks, the TEM-vs-PEC shot comparison and the circuit/application function split all match the English. There are a few naturalness slips. "utility-grade performance" is calqued as "performances à l'échelle utilitaire", and "computational scientists" as "scientifiques computationnels". In [30], "facilement" appears three times: it is added to "swap in" ("intégrer facilement") and then repeated. [68] has a stiff double relative clause ("qui applique ... qui permettent").

examples.source: to make utility-grade performance accessible out of the box. This allows computational scientists to focus
examples.translation: pour offrir d'emblée des performances à l'échelle utilitaire. Cela permet aux scientifiques computationnels de se concentrer
examples.suggested: pour offrir d'emblée des performances de niveau utilitaire (utility-scale). Cela permet aux chercheurs en calcul scientifique de se concentrer
examples.why: 'à l'échelle utilitaire' and 'scientifiques computationnels' are calques that a French technical writer would not use.

examples.source: allows you to swap in new tools ... readily deployable ... where you can easily leverage classical compute
examples.translation: te permet d'intégrer facilement de nouveaux outils ... également facilement déployables ... où tu peux facilement exploiter le calcul classique
examples.suggested: te permet de substituer de nouveaux outils ... directement déployables ... où tu peux facilement exploiter le calcul classique
examples.why: 'facilement' appears three times in two sentences. The first one is not in the source ('swap in' means substitute), which gives the prose a repetitive, machine-translated feel.

examples.source: applies AI-driven quantum control techniques, with which users can scale successfully to larger problems
examples.translation: qui applique des techniques de contrôle quantique pilotées par l'IA, qui permettent aux utilisateurs de passer avec succès à des problèmes de plus grande taille
examples.suggested: qui applique des techniques de contrôle quantique pilotées par l'IA, grâce auxquelles les utilisateurs peuvent passer à des problèmes de plus grande taille
examples.why: The two 'qui' clauses in a row read stiffly.

editor_note: Faithful across all five short entries: "skills" is rendered consistently as "compétences" (a defensible choice), "changelog" as "Journal des modifications", and entry [5] keeps the meaning that the migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime skill was released for migrating code ("a été publiée, pour migrer le code").

The meaning is faithful throughout. The hedge "might be faster" correctly becomes "pourraient être plus rapides", and the informal "tu" is used consistently (Consulte, visite, Lis). There are two small naturalness slips. In [6], "visite les notes de version" copies the English "visit"; French would use "consulte", which also avoids the clumsy "version… versions… version". In [9], "leurs Qiskit patterns et workflows actuels" keeps English word order and reads awkwardly.

examples.source: To see the release notes for all versions, visit the Qiskit Transpiler Service client release notes.
examples.translation: Pour consulter les notes de version de toutes les versions, visite les [notes de version du client Qiskit Transpiler Service]
examples.suggested: Les notes de version de toutes les versions sont disponibles dans les [notes de version du client Qiskit Transpiler Service].
examples.why: "Visiter" a document copies the English "visit"; French uses "consulter" or "voir". The sentence also repeats "version" three times.

examples.source: integrate the service into their current Qiskit patterns and workflows
examples.translation: intégrer facilement le service dans leurs Qiskit patterns et workflows actuels
examples.suggested: intégrer facilement le service dans leurs workflows et leurs Qiskit patterns existants
examples.why: The English phrase is dropped in right after the possessive ("leurs Qiskit patterns"), with "actuels" trailing ambiguously. Reordering reads more naturally in French.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and uses "tu" throughout ("Écris", "Consulte", "Tu te demandes"). Nothing in it would mislead a learner. There are two small slips. In [9], "Rust-driven performance enhancements" becomes "gains de performance grâce à une réécriture en Rust", which says the code was rewritten in Rust when the source only says the improvements are Rust-driven. The product name also changes word order: "Qiskit SDK" in [1] versus "SDK Qiskit" in [0] and [15].

examples.source: Upgrades and Rust-driven performance enhancements to `VF2Layout` and `VF2PostLayout`
examples.translation: Des mises à niveau et des gains de performance grâce à une réécriture en Rust pour `VF2Layout` et `VF2PostLayout`
examples.suggested: Des mises à niveau et des gains de performance portés par Rust pour `VF2Layout` et `VF2PostLayout`
examples.why: The source doesn't mention a rewrite. It only says the performance gains come from Rust. The claim is slightly strengthened, though it doesn't really mislead.

examples.translation: Journal des modifications du Qiskit SDK
examples.suggested: Journal des modifications du SDK Qiskit
examples.why: The word order doesn't match [0] and [15], which both use "SDK Qiskit". "du Qiskit SDK" also reads awkwardly in French.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Dates, quantities (1 µs vs 250 µs, 68 ns vs 138 ns, 20-2000 µs), negations and caveats such as "not yet supported" and "no sooner than" all match the English, and the tu register holds. The problems are for a native editor, not a learner. "Timing" is rendered three ways: "synchronisation" in [17], "temporisation" in [266] and a bare "timing" in [167]/[169]. "Synchronisation" is also the wrong idea for a schedule chart. "Mid-circuit" appears as both "en cours de circuit" ([11], [57], [90]) and "en milieu de circuit" ([264]). The "Compute resources" page name is sometimes translated ("Ressources de calcul", [143], [146], [190]) and sometimes kept in English ([104], [113], [114]), and first-of-month dates switch between "1er" and a bare "1" ([174], [175], [221], [276]). There are also a few calques, such as "tu es le bienvenu pour créer" [251], "environnement d'exécution runtime" [45] and "pendant quelques jours pendant que" [160].

examples.source: **Circuit timing chart** — shows a scheduled timeline of a circuit's operations
examples.translation: **Graphique de synchronisation du circuit** — affiche une chronologie programmée
examples.suggested: **Chronogramme du circuit** (or « Graphique de timing du circuit »)
examples.why: 'Timing' here means scheduling and durations, not synchronisation. The same concept is 'temporisation' in [266] and 'timing' in [167], so the file uses three renderings.

examples.translation: Amélioration de la mesure en milieu de circuit
examples.suggested: Amélioration de la mesure en cours de circuit
examples.why: Everywhere else ([11], [57], [90], [121]) the file uses 'en cours de circuit', so this is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: We plan to retire `ibm_brisbane` on or around 1 November 2025.
examples.why: French writes the first of the month as '1er'. The file does this correctly in [107] and [203] but not in [175], [221] or [276].

examples.source: you are welcome to create a free Open Plan account
examples.translation: tu es le bienvenu pour créer un compte gratuit Open Plan
examples.suggested: n'hésite pas à créer un compte Open Plan gratuit
examples.why: This is a calque of 'you are welcome to'. A French writer would say 'n'hésite pas à'.

examples.source: you might only see the English version of recently released content for a few days while the translation is underway
examples.translation: donc tu pourrais ne voir que la version anglaise du contenu récemment publié pendant quelques jours pendant que la traduction est en cours
examples.suggested: tu risques de ne voir que la version anglaise des contenus récents pendant quelques jours, le temps que la traduction soit terminée
examples.why: 'pendant … pendant que' repeats itself and reads as stiff, translated syntax.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The beta caveat and the qiskit-ibm-runtime ≥ 0.47.0 requirement are kept, and the TREX, PEC and shaded-lightcone techniques are rendered correctly. The informal "tu" register holds. Two wording calques are worth fixing: "helper class" became "classe d'assistance" where French developers say "classe utilitaire", and "visit the release notes" became "visite les notes de version" where "consulte" is the natural verb, as the page already uses in [13].

examples.source: a new version of the noise-learning helper class, `NoiseLearnerV3`
examples.translation: une nouvelle version de la classe d'assistance à l'apprentissage du bruit, `NoiseLearnerV3`
examples.suggested: une nouvelle version de la classe utilitaire d'apprentissage du bruit, `NoiseLearnerV3`
examples.why: Literal calque of 'helper class'. The usual French software term is 'classe utilitaire'.

examples.source: To see the release notes for all versions, visit the IBM Quantum Compute client release notes.
examples.translation: Pour consulter les notes de version de toutes les versions, visite les notes de version du client IBM Quantum Compute.
examples.suggested: Les notes de version de toutes les versions sont disponibles dans les notes de version du client IBM Quantum Compute.
examples.why: 'Visiter' used for documentation is an anglicism. The sentence also repeats 'notes de version' and 'version(s)', which reads stiffly.
